title: Diminishing-return Burst Controller — PRD (draft)
content:
Purpose / elevator pitch:
We need a burst mechanism that (a) lets tenants handle real short-lived surges, (b) prevents a small set of aggressive tenants from permanently consuming shared headroom, and (c) plays nicely with reserved capacity and the autoscaler. The proposed Diminishing-Return Burst Controller (DRBC) makes each burst token/credit progressively less effective the more the tenant relies on it over a short rolling window. This preserves burst experience for intermittent spikes while nudging high-consumption tenants toward Dedicated reservations or sustained scaling.

Context / motivation:
- Current burst systems either give flat credits (easy to game) or strictly cap bursts (poor UX for genuine spikes).
- We want to balance latency SLOs and fairness without creating churny preemption/eviction behavior.
- DRBC intends to be an ops-friendly layer between credit accounting and active routing/fallbacks.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce multi-tenant headroom hogging incidents by >= 40% in top-10 noisy neighbor cases (90th pct tail).
- Keep median burst latency impact < 10% vs baseline for genuine 30s spikes.
- Limit churn: retries/preemptions caused by burst exhaustion should not increase > 5% for healthy tenants.

Non-goals:
- DRBC is not a long-term pricing redesign. It’s an operational mitigation and product signal.
- We will not replace reserved-contract logic; DRBC should respect reservation anchors and SLA bands.

High-level design:
1) Credit accrual: tenants accrue burst credits under existing rules (e.g., per-minute accrual based on plan). No change here.
2) Effectiveness curve: when credits are consumed, each credit's effective capacity contribution is multiplied by a decay factor that depends on recent consumption density. Early credits in a window are full-value; subsequent credits are scaled down (diminishing returns).
3) Rolling window and decay shape: default window = 30 minutes; decay is exponential with shape parameter k. Effective_capacity = nominal_credit * exp(-k * cumulative_consumption_fraction).
4) Soft caps and soft-fallbacks: when effective_capacity falls below a per-tenant soft threshold, the controller triggers graded responses: a) hint to client (X-Rate-Limit advising reduced burst), b) route low-priority requests to lower-cost/model variants, c) start autoscaler prewarm/commit suggestions to tenant admin UI.
5) Reservation respect: tenants with reserved capacity (Dedicated) get a higher baseline and slower decay; DRBC must not reduce reserved capacity below contractual levels.

Why diminishing returns?
- Provides natural economic pressure without hard cutoffs.
- Encourages tenants with sustained high bursts to move to predictable capacity or improve traffic shaping.
- Smoother operational footprint: avoids hard evictions that ripple through multi-tenant pools.

User stories / examples:
- Sporadic spike: App A has a 20s spike; DRBC gives full credit — outcome: latency preserved, negligible decay.
- Repeated microbursts: App B sends a burst every 2 minutes over 30m; later bursts see reduced effectiveness -> App B observes slightly slower throughput and receives UI hints to apply rate-limit or request Dedicated.
- Noisy neighbor: Top noisy tenant repeatedly consumes burst headroom; DRBC throttles marginal effectiveness causing system-wide headroom to be preserved for others.

Simple pseudocode (controller-side):
  // per-tenant state: credit_balance, recent_consumption (time-decayed), reserved_baseline
  window = 30m
  k = default_decay (configurable, e.g. 0.8)
  on_request(req):
    nominal = min(req.tokens, credit_balance + spare_soft_headroom)
    fraction = recent_consumption / window_capacity_estimate
    effective = nominal * exp(-k * fraction)
    apply_tokens(effective)
    recent_consumption += effective (decay recent_consumption over time)
    if effective < nominal * 0.6: emit_hint_and_consider_fallback(req)
Operational considerations:
- Telemetry: exposure of nominal vs effective token throughput per tenant, recent_consumption metric, decay parameter k per pool, and number of hint/fallback events.
- Rollout: start with canary on 2 internal tenants and one small customer-facing pool for 2 weeks. Compare headroom tail metrics and customer-facing error rates.
- Experiment knobs: window size, decay k, soft threshold multiplier, and prewarm lead time. We should evolve these per pool type (CPU-backed vs GPU, shared vs soft-slice).
- Interaction with autoscaler: when DRBC engages (sustained reduced effectiveness), emit a signal to autoscaler as a soft demand escalation (not immediate escalate to full reservation). Autoscaler then can choose to prewarm or recommend reserved capacity.

Isolation controls and safety nets:
- Safety floor: never let DRBC reduce reserved contractual baseline.
- Emergency override: SRE-runbook with TTL overrides for paging and debug (one-click bypass for 15m). All overrides audited.
- Fairness audit job: nightly job ranks tenants by effective credit discounting to detect misconfigs or abuse (alerts to CS/Account).

Failover and fallback policy suggestions:
- Tiered fallbacks: 1) route to quantized model variant (lower GPU memory, higher throughput), 2) degrade max tokens per request for best-effort calls, 3) route to regional replica with spare capacity (if allowed by data policy).
- User-visible UX: when we issue a hint, include lightweight telemetry in the admin console: "In last 30m your burst efficiency averaged 46% — consider enabling reserved capacity or smoothing requests."

Metrics to track (telemetry):
- Headroom preservation: 95th/99th percentile free headroom minutes per pool pre/post rollout.
- Tenant credit effectiveness distribution: median, p75, p90, p99.
- Customer-visible latency and error rate for canary tenants.
- Hints-to-action conversion: % of tenants who acted on hint within 7 days (clicked recommended path).

Backward compat / migration:
- Default state for existing tenants: DRBC off. Feature-flag gate per pool with gradual enable.
- For customers with explicit contractual SLOs, allow opt-out via contract tag. Opt-outs must be logged and reviewed by Finance/Legal.

Implementation notes and rough effort estimate:
- Controller logic: 2-3 sprint engineers (product + eng) to implement decay calculation, credit-effectiveness telemetry, and hint/event plumbing.
- Console UI changes: add hint banner and a "Request capacity" quick-flow — 1 designer + 1 FE engineer (1 sprint).
- Autoscaler integration: signal bridge (protobuf + metric) 1-2 eng sprints.
- SRE runbook and override tool: 0.5 sprint.
Total: ~4-6 sprints across small cross-functional team for MVP.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Window sizing: 30m is a guess. Longer windows preserve occasional back-to-back bursts, shorter windows harshen repeated spikes. We should A/B test 15m vs 30m vs 60m.
- Decay curvature: exponential gives nice math but a piecewise-linear curve might be more interpretable to customers. Recommendation: implement both curves behind a flag and test.
- Economic signals: Should discounts or billing adjustments be tied to DRBC events? For now, keep separate; use DRBC telemetry to inform potential pricing experiments later.
- Edge-case: burst-heavy but low-cost embeddings / short-response workloads — we should treat by token-cost or model-fingerprint since not all tokens are equal in cost.

Security & compliance notes:
- Ensure any tenant hints or usage summaries exposed in the console do not include cross-tenant telemetry. Per-tenant aggregated metrics only.

Rollout plan (high-level):
- Week 0: implementation merged behind feature flag; unit + load tests
- Week 1-2: internal canary (engineering org) across 2 pools; iterate on k/window defaults.
- Week 3-4: invite opt-in customers + 1 small paid pool; track metrics daily.
- Week 5: broader opt-in; update console UX; prepare public docs.
- Week 8: GA for shared pools if telemetry >= goals.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- [Aisha] draft initial server-side change list and push RFC to eng-architecture (due 2025-11-18).
- [Marco] implement telemetry primitives and nightly fairness audit prototype (due 2025-11-26).
- [Lena] quick UI mockups for hint banner + capacity recommendation flow (draft by 2025-11-20).
- [Devon] propose autoscaler signal schema and proto (draft by 2025-11-25).

Notes to self / working thoughts:
- Might be useful to include a short runaway-detection submodule that forces a grace-cooldown if tenant demonstrates sustained >x% of pool capacity over y minutes.
- Need to consider multi-region tenants and cross-region headroom coordination (hard). Start single-region first.
- Keep the messaging soft and educational: "Your burst worked, but repeated bursts are expensive; try these options" rather than punitive language.

References / related tickets:
- DEDIC-1428 (linked) — initial customer report of noisy-burst behavior
- DEDIC-1373 — autoscaler prewarm suggestion proto (early draft)
- design notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DED/pages/2048/diminishing-return-burst-controller

End of draft.

(feel free to rip out any section and replace — this is intentionally rough; need engineering eyes on telemetry shapes and on how to respect reserved-contract anchors.)
